worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{6}^{0}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{6}(5f(x)+1)\,\text{d}x & =5{\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{0}^{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(-4)\,+\,x\,{|}_{0}^{6} \\  & =-20\,+\,(6-0) \\  & =-20\,+\,6 \\  & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$
